questions.stem: Which particle completes 「だれ___そう言いましたか。」 ('Who said that?')?
questions.explanation: A question word that is the subject always takes が: だれが, 何が. は marks something already known as the topic, and a question word is by definition unknown.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「春子さん___作ったケーキはおいしかったです。」?
questions.explanation: Inside a clause that describes a noun (春子さんが作ったケーキ, 'the cake Haruko made'), the subject takes が, not は. The topic of the whole sentence is the cake, which already has は.

questions.stem: In 「肉は食べますが、魚は食べません。」, what does the second は do?
options: It marks fish as the subject of 食べません.
It turns the sentence into a question.
It shows that fish belongs to someone.
questions.explanation: は can mark contrast: 'meat I eat, but fish I don't'. The subject, the speaker, is understood and not stated; fish is what is eaten, not who eats.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「ねこはつくえ___下にいます。」 ('The cat is under the desk')?
questions.explanation: Position words are nouns, so they join the object with の: つくえの下, 'the underneath of the desk'. The に comes after the position word, marking where the cat is.

questions.stem: What does 「日本語の先生」 mean?
options: a teacher who is in Japan
a teacher of the Japanese language
questions.explanation: の links two nouns, and the first describes the second: 日本語の先生 is a teacher of Japanese. A teacher who is Japanese would be 日本人の先生, and 'the teacher's Japanese' reverses the order: 先生の日本語.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「駅の前___大きい本屋があります。」?
questions.explanation: あります and います take に for the place where something is: 駅の前にあります. で marks the place where an action happens, and being somewhere is not an action.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「としょかん___本を読みました。」 ('I read a book at the library')?
questions.explanation: Reading is an action, so its place takes で: としょかんで読みました. に marks where something exists or where you go, so it would need a verb such as あります or 行きます.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「先生___手紙を書きました。」 ('I wrote a letter to my teacher')?
questions.explanation: The person who receives something is the indirect object, marked with に: 先生に書きました. を already marks the letter, the thing written, and a sentence like this has only one を.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「デパートへ買い物___行きました。」 ('I went shopping at the department store')?
questions.explanation: With a verb of motion, に marks the purpose of going: 買い物に行きました, 'went for shopping'. へ already marks where they went, and 買い物を would need a verb like する, not 行く.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「この道___まっすぐ行ってください。」 ('Please go straight along this road')?
questions.explanation: With verbs of movement, を marks the space you move along or through: 道を行く, 道を歩く. に would mark a destination, and the road is the route, not where you end up.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「電車___学校に行きます。」 ('I go to school by train')?
questions.explanation: で marks the means by which something is done: 電車で, 'by train'. に is used with 乗る (電車に乗る, 'get on a train'), but not to show how you travel.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「家族___日本に行きました。」 ('I went to Japan with my family')?
questions.explanation: と marks the person you do something with: 家族と, 'with my family'. へ marks direction, and the sentence already has its destination, 日本に.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「スーパーでりんご___バナナを買いました。」 to mean 'apples, bananas and other things'?
questions.explanation: や lists examples and implies there were other things too. と lists everything: りんごとバナナ would be just apples and bananas.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「ペン___えんぴつをとってください。」 ('Please pass me a pen or a pencil')?
questions.explanation: か between nouns means 'or': ペンかえんぴつ. と and や both mean 'and', which would ask for both.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「だれ___来ましたか。」 ('Did someone come?')?
questions.explanation: A question word plus か makes an indefinite word: だれか, 'someone'. だれが来ましたか would ask 'Who came?', a different question that expects a name in reply.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「だれ___来ませんでした。」 ('Nobody came')?
questions.explanation: A question word plus も with a negative verb is 'no one', 'nothing' or 'nowhere': だれも来ませんでした. だれか is 'someone', which does not give 'nobody'.

questions.stem: What does 「京都には何回も行きました。」 mean?
options: I have never been to Kyoto.
I went to Kyoto only once.
I have been to Kyoto many times.
How many times have you been to Kyoto?
questions.explanation: With a counter and a positive verb, 何 plus も stresses a large number: 何回も, 'many times'. Without も, 何回 would ask how many times.

questions.stem: Which pair completes 「家には犬___ねこ___いません。」 ('There is neither a dog nor a cat at home')?
questions.explanation: も after each noun with a negative verb means 'neither … nor': 犬もねこもいません. With a positive verb the same pattern means 'both … and'.

questions.stem: Which words complete 「金曜日___しゅくだいを出してください。」 ('Please hand in your homework by Friday')?
questions.explanation: までに is a deadline, 'by': 金曜日までに出す. まで is 'until' and goes with an action that continues up to that time, but handing something in happens once.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「五時___としょかんで勉強しました。」 ('I studied at the library until five')?
questions.explanation: Studying goes on over a period, so its end point takes まで, 'until'. までに is a deadline for something done once, such as 五時までに帰ります, 'be home by five'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「毎日、二時間___勉強します。」 ('I study for about two hours every day')?
questions.explanation: ぐらい (or くらい) is 'about' with an amount or a length of time: 二時間ぐらい. ごろ is 'about' only with a point in time, as in 三時ごろ, 'around three o'clock'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「千円___ありません。」 ('I only have a thousand yen')?
questions.explanation: しか means 'only' and must be followed by a negative: 千円しかありません. だけ also means 'only', but it takes a positive verb, so with ありません it cannot mean 'I only have'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「きょうだいは姉が一人___です。」 ('My only sibling is one older sister')?
questions.explanation: だけ means 'only' with a positive ending: 一人だけです. しか would need a negative verb, as in 一人しかいません.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「電車はバス___高いです。」 ('The train is more expensive than the bus')?
questions.explanation: より marks the thing being compared against, 'than': バスより高い. から and まで mark starting and finishing points, not comparisons.

questions.stem: How do you say 'I like summer the best'?
options: 夏が一番より好きです。
questions.explanation: 一番 goes straight before the adjective for 'the most': 一番好き. より is 'than' and needs something to compare with; it is never added to 一番.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「きのうは雨でした___、海に行きました。」 ('It rained yesterday, but I went to the beach')?
questions.explanation: After a full clause, が is the conjunction 'but': 雨でしたが. から and ので give a reason, which would make the rain the cause of going to the beach.

questions.stem: What does 「いっしょうけんめい勉強したけれども、テストができませんでした。」 mean?
options: Because I studied hard, I did well in the test.
I studied hard so that I would do well in the test.
I didn't study, so I didn't do well in the test.
Although I studied hard, I didn't do well in the test.
questions.explanation: けれども joins two clauses with 'although' or 'however', so the second clause runs against what the first leads you to expect. 'Because' would be から or ので.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「すみません、あたまがいたい___、今日は休みます。」 ('Sorry, I have a headache, so I'll take today off')?
questions.explanation: ので gives a reason and is the usual choice for a polite excuse. のに and けれども introduce something that goes against expectation, which the headache does not.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「雨がふっていた___、友だちは駅まで来てくれました。」 ('Even though it was raining, my friend came all the way to the station')?
questions.explanation: のに is 'even though', and it carries a feeling that the result is surprising or touching. ので and から would make the rain the reason the friend came.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「雨がふる___すずしくなります。」 ('Whenever it rains, it gets cooler')?
questions.explanation: と after the dictionary form is the conditional for something that always follows: 'when it rains, it gets cooler'. のに, けれども and が all mean 'but' or 'although', which turns a natural result into a contrast.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「先生は来週テストがある___言いました。」?
questions.explanation: と marks what was said or thought before 言う and 思う: テストがあると言いました, 'said that there is a test'. を can mark a noun that is said (名前を言う), but not a whole clause.

questions.stem: Which particle completes 「りょうりをする___は楽しいです。」 ('Cooking is fun')?
questions.explanation: の after a plain verb turns the action into a noun, 'cooking', which can then be the topic with は. を and が mark nouns, but they cannot turn a verb into one.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「しゅみは本を読む___です。」 ('My hobby is reading books')?
questions.explanation: Both の and こと turn a verb into a noun, but before です in 'X is …' only こと is used: しゅみは読むことです. の works as a subject or topic (読むのは楽しい) but not here.

questions.stem: Which words complete 「私は漢字を書く___できます。」 ('I can write kanji')?
questions.explanation: Ability is the dictionary form plus ことができる, with が because できる takes が for what can be done. ことを and ことに appear in other structures, such as ことにする.

questions.stem: What does 「来年、日本に行くことにしました。」 mean?
options: I can go to Japan next year.
I went to Japan last year.
I've decided to go to Japan next year.
It has been arranged that I'll go to Japan next year.
questions.explanation: ことにする is a decision the speaker makes: 'I've decided to go'. ことになる is a decision made by others or by circumstances, so 'it has been arranged' would need 行くことになりました.

questions.stem: What does 「父の仕事で、京都に住むことになりました。」 mean?
options: Because of my father's job, I've decided to live in Kyoto.
My father has decided to find a job in Kyoto.
My father can live in Kyoto because of his job.
Because of my father's job, it's been settled that we'll live in Kyoto.
questions.explanation: ことになる reports an outcome decided by circumstances or other people, here the father's job. 'I've decided' would be ことにしました, the speaker's own choice.

questions.stem: You and a friend have just stepped outside together. Which particle completes 「今日はさむいです___。」 to invite agreement?
questions.explanation: ね asks the listener to agree with something you both know, like 'isn't it?'. よ tells the listener something they don't know yet, which is odd when they feel the cold too.

questions.stem: Your friend doesn't know when the film starts. Which particle completes 「えいがは七時からです___。」 to tell them?
questions.explanation: よ gives the listener new information, 'I'm telling you'. ね would assume the friend already knows and is being asked to agree.

questions.stem: In casual speech, what does the の do in 「日本に行ったことがあるの？」?
options: It marks the object of the verb.
It puts the verb in the past.
It makes a soft, friendly question.
questions.explanation: With rising intonation, の at the end makes a gentle casual question, 'Have you been to Japan?'. か at the end of a plain-form question sounds abrupt in everyday speech, so の is the natural choice.

questions.stem: Which counter completes 「えんぴつが三___あります。」?
questions.explanation: 本 counts long, thin things: pencils, bottles, umbrellas, trees, so three pencils are 三本 (さんぼん). 〜まい is for flat things such as paper, stamps and shirts.

questions.stem: Which counter completes 「きってを五___買いました。」?
questions.explanation: 〜まい counts flat, thin things: stamps, sheets of paper, tickets, shirts, so five stamps are 五まい. 本 is for long, thin things such as pencils.

questions.stem: Which counter completes 「ねこが二___います。」?
questions.explanation: 〜ひき counts small animals such as cats, dogs and fish: 二ひき, with the sound changing in 一ぴき and 三びき. 人 is only for people.

questions.stem: Which completes 「りんごを___ください。」 ('Two apples, please')?
questions.explanation: つ is the general counter for objects with no special counter, such as apples: 二つ, read ふたつ. 本 is for long, thin things like bananas or bottles.

questions.stem: Which counter completes 「弟は十二___です。」 ('My younger brother is twelve')?
questions.explanation: 才 counts years of age: 十二才, 'twelve years old'. 番 is for numbers in a sequence, as in 三番, 'number three'.

questions.stem: Which counter completes 「一週間に二___テニスをします。」 ('I play tennis twice a week')?
questions.explanation: 回 counts times or occasions: 二回, 'twice'. 番 gives a position in order, 'number two', not how often something happens.
